⟦0⟧ Expected number of factories put on Consumer Goods
**In 1939 scenario, if ⟦0⟧ is released as ⟦1⟧, it will only have its civilian factory but no military factory, and instead it is given extra 2 ⟦2⟧.
**In 1936 scenario, ⟦0⟧ has access on ⟦1⟧ oil and extra amounts if ⟦2⟧ upgrades its infrastructure and research.

**By Blood Alone Update, in 1939 scenario, if ⟦0⟧ is released ny ⟦1⟧'s decision, it will get the Oil access back. Should ⟦2⟧ take the Albanian related focuses, ⟦3⟧ gains additional oil and gets 1 amount of Rubber.
**At this point, it would have 12 Oil, 1 Rubber, 4 Aluminium and 6 Chromium.
* marks a division that is removed in the 1939 start. ^ marks a division only available via decision.
Albania has a tiny military. It starts with 1 unit in 1936, being an Infantry Division unit.
If released via an Italian decision, it gets two infantry units stationed in Tiranë and Korçë.
These unites have a unique template, which cannot be removed or switched. No new units of this template can be recruited.
The below is ⟦0⟧ player suggested strategies for ⟦1⟧. Bear in mind, due to the dynamic nature of the game, it may unfold differently for other players.

Though ⟦0⟧ is in a better situation than ⟦1⟧ (another nation under threat of annexation), the improvement of survivability is very thin. With a very small population, unlikely ever to expand, it's clear that interventionist branch of liberty ethos is completely inadequate at best and a burden at worst.

The best option to improve your army performance against ⟦0⟧ is to build coastal forts and just in case land forts (should ⟦1⟧ naval invade around the port). But even then ⟦2⟧ can simply go through ⟦3⟧, and there's very little ⟦4⟧ can do unless it went to the nationalism branch. In every ideology, except Democratic, ⟦5⟧ will try to invade you.

So the best survival strategy is to turn fascist and try to join the ⟦0⟧ before ⟦1⟧ either attacks or joins the Axis first. Once the Anschluss is done, both of them have a direct land border, so the war will probably end with ⟦2⟧ utterly defeated, thereby removing your only active threat. It is unlikely that you will be able to claim many Italian provinces though.

After that, if you're feeling lucky and world tension is still low, maybe try and declare war on ⟦0⟧ or ⟦1⟧. The rest of the Axis will do most of the heavy lifting, but with this being a land war you should be able to actually get some war score to make claims. Although it does have the potential to rope you into a war with the allies, so keep that in mind. Then you can leave the Axis and build your army. Being a fascist nation allows your to implement war economy on industry and higher conscription laws in peacetime, while the national focus provide massive manpower boosts.

⟦0⟧ is yet another nation that threatens with invasion. A lesser scenario compared to Italy's usual campaign. Again, like with Italy's case, in every ideology, except Democratic they will justify on you. And, this occurs when ⟦1⟧ hasn't declared war on you for a considerate amount of time, or has become Democratic. First things first, start to build forts and just in case coastal forts, as ⟦2⟧ will try to attack from both south and from the west coast.

Like in the Italian strategy, you can turn fascist and try to join the ⟦0⟧ before ⟦1⟧ attacks or joins the Allies or Axis. Since ⟦2⟧ has a tendency to join either, no matter the ideology. Or alternatively turn communist and try to join the ⟦3⟧. The latter is more beneficial, as the ⟦4⟧ will try to engage in naval invasion to distract ⟦5⟧ from the North Epirus campaign, and turn on the defensive. After that, if you're feeling lucky try to make some pushing, being a land war you should be able to actually get some war score to make claims. And in this case, taking most of Epirus, Macedonia, Thrace and Athens.

One rare occurrence is if Bulgaria has completed 'Support Macedonian Organizations' and if Albania happens to own Central Macedonia and Thrace, take the decisions to suppress the IMRO activities and somehow you'll gain cores on those areas.

Another viable strategy is to turn communist after finishing 'Internationalism focus', where you hold a referendum into communism and rush until 'Indoctrination'. Though this will require either both ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ to turn communist or ⟦2⟧ to join the Comintern.

Though it has been annexed, as either as non aligned or fascist ⟦0⟧, ⟦1⟧ gets a second chance to relive itself rather as a puppet state. But in this case, with extra features that as an independent country it doesn't have. A national spirit that helps with the manpower issue, two extra cores notably on ⟦2⟧ ⟦3⟧ and ⟦4⟧ ⟦5⟧, two infantry units and regained oil access from ⟦6⟧. Should the player stay a bit longer as ⟦7⟧ just to complete Albanian focuses, territorial claims and extra oil with rubber resources, the thin improvement of the country is better than none. Considering that AI ⟦8⟧ will likely neglect the Albanian focuses and go with its own buffs. With a very small population, the situation as before annexation remains almost as same as before. Unlike annexation threat, the path of independence is the main priority as ⟦9⟧ has to regain its independence by any of their means. Either remaining fascist, or by civil war.

As it has been done historically, one way to rebel from your overlord is to go communist. Since reinstating King Zog back to its throne is impossible and if the Axis campaign, or the Italian led faction, isn't progressing in their favour then it is better to continue with communist advisors. In 1939 scenario, ⟦0⟧ inherits Italy's infantry templates, and has two starting infantry units, it has to start training the cheapest infantry unit to gain ground. Do not spawn them yet until the civil war starts or/and the Axis is facing difficulties, and it is getting pushed by the ⟦1⟧. Focus on the political side before the industry, as losing building slots to the civil war will be a wasted focus. You gain Enver Hoxha, a leader with a decent trait, and enough ground to seize Tirana unopposed with your army at the ready. Join the Comintern and assist the ⟦2⟧ with the Balkan campaign. If Bashkimi Kombëtar decision was done by ⟦3⟧, then the focus is to gain the claimed lands in your domain notably if they are under Axis control.

Another historical dissidence but had insignificant support than the communist one, is the democratic resistance. Again, like with the communist scenario, it will have to resort to civil war. Unlike with Hoxha, the leader is rather generic without a trait, so the choice is completely inadequate at best. The sole benefit is diplomatically, as it gets to join the Allies, and if ⟦0⟧ has joined the Allies, there is a chance that if ⟦1⟧ capitulates to the Axis, it will be prone to naval invasion(in this case liberation) committed by Allied troops.

Although it is long and during, staying as fascist ⟦0⟧ has its own features if the player doesn't wish to resort to civil war and change ideology. With a leader that vaguely contributes to less costly independence, two small units and a small industry, the first choice to focus first on industry. As producing guns and convoys, will certainly go to land lease to the overlord to gain independence points. Make sure to spawn enough infantry units to defend your coast as the Allied troops have a tendency to naval invade ⟦1⟧ first, before going after ⟦2⟧. If it's assumed safety on the coast, ⟦3⟧ can also train a few troops to assist with any major campaign that the ⟦4⟧ or ⟦5⟧ are holding. This, the resource exporting and land lease to overlord will certainly contribute to independence, whether if it is slow.

In this case scenario, it happens when neither ⟦0⟧ or ⟦1⟧ don't threaten you with war for a long period, and they have taken "Democratic" paths that don't involve conquering ⟦2⟧. With this much time given to ⟦3⟧, all that you need to do is to rush down to either Fascism or Communism to assert control upon the Balkans. Otherwise, should the player opt for a peaceful gameplay then it can opt staying non-aligned or democratic and make slight improvements on the country that can take months.

Now, the first thing you should do is take the first Political focus, which will give you 120 political power, plus the 70 you have already accumulated. Use this to get a communist advisor. Yes, I know, going communist is the go-to strategy for basically every minor, but if it works, it works. While you wait for communist support to tick up, take some industrial focuses to get some free factories. Grab the two free civilian factories first, then get the three military factories. By this time you should be above fifty percent communist support, so hold a referendum to become Socialist Republic of Albania. Use your excess political power to get war economy, and if you have any extra left, get some Improved Worker Conditions or Anti-Communist/Democratic raids. Should you have any chief of army advisor, get it in order to boost some army experience, and get the "Ideological Loyalty" Spirit of the Army, and complete the "Indoctrination" Focus for extra manpower. Since Albania's population pales with the rest of the Balkans average population.

By now you should have a total of 5 or 6 factories- 3 civilian and 4 military. One of your civilian factories will be used for consumer goods, so use the remaining one to either build some more civs or trade for some steel. Use one of your 3 military factories to produce artillery, and use the other 2 to build guns. Set some factories to build support equipment as well once you get some more mils.

At this point, you should've flipped communist already, so start justifying on ⟦0⟧. At the same time start working on the political focuses. Make a template of one cavalry unit, and spam it out. You should also have a fair amount of political power at this point, so take some stability-increasing decisions. Should you declare on ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧, or god forbid, ⟦3⟧ and win against them each other can give you enough expansion and access to some valuable resources and sea access for marine trade.
